items.title: The functor of points where a module is flat in dimensions at least n is an fpqc sheaf and limit preserving
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the functor F_n of points where the module is flat in dimensions at least n on the fibres is an fpqc sheaf, and is limit preserving when the morphism is quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation and the module is of finite presentation (statement lines 6336-6345, tag 05MV). The proof splits into a short sheaf argument comparing the two non flat loci through flat base change and a genuinely longer limit argument: it first reduces to a morphism of finite presentation over an affine base using finite affine coverings, and then approximates the non flat locus by a finitely presented closed subscheme whose fibres have dimension below n, descends it together with the dimension bound and with flatness off it, and uses quasi-compactness of the complement to conclude. The approximation and descent step is the substance, so the claim is H2.
